rule:
The headroom of every room, access route and circulation space must be at least 2.0 m; at a doorway it is measured to the underside of the transom.

Regulatory text (the authoritative clauses - use them to interpret the requirement and its applicability; you must still work out how to read or measure it from the IFC):
BCA Approved Document (Acceptable Solutions) V7.08:
C.3.2.1 The headroom of every room, access route and circulation space shall not be less than 2.0 metres.
Note: 1 The term “access route” shall include a covered walkway or footway of a building. 2 The headroom is measured from the finished floor level to - a) in the case of a doorway, the underside of the transom; ... c) in all other cases, the underside of any beam, duct, service pipe, fixture, fitting or other obstruction or projection.
Authority IFC convention (headroom test summary): the underside of the transom is the door's recorded ClearHeight in its IFC-SG door property set.
Benchmark policy: every doorway is assessed; the room exemptions (attics, plant rooms, small stores, owner-built houses) do not exempt a doorway.

Label every door.
Report the GlobalId of every element (modelled as IfcDoor) that does NOT satisfy this requirement.
notes: Doorway headroom of the 157 template doors: {'FAIL': 3, 'PASS': 154}; 33 lift doors outside the template are unscored.
